html:
The Patamona and Ingarikó are closely related Cariban-speaking peoples of the Pakaraima Mountains, where Guyana, Brazil and Venezuela meet. Together with the Akawaio they are often grouped as the Kapon.

Their land is a highland of table mountains, savannas and forest around Mount Roraima, and it includes Kaieteur Falls, one of the highest single-drop waterfalls in the world. They farm cassava in forest gardens, hunt and fish. In the 1800s many of them took up Hallelujah, a religion that mixes Christian and local ideas and spread among the Kapon and the Pemon. Their languages belong to the Cariban family.
